doc.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004

title: Opening, introduction and the band's wide audience
summary: Copyright notice, biographical notes and Monk Rowe's welcome. Rowe notes that his whole family likes the music; Fleck is glad it reaches all ages.

Béla Fleck was born in New York City on July 10, 1958. He has transformed the traditional role of the banjo while creating his own distinctive musical genre with the Flecktones. Béla has enjoyed musical collaborations with artists such as Bruce Hornsby, Chic Corea and Branford Marsalis, and he has received multiple Grammy awards for his recordings and compositions.
Béla was interviewed before a performance at Hamilton in Clinton on December 7, 2004 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.
We are filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive on campus and I’m really pleased to have Béla Fleck with me today. Welcome.
Thank you. Nice to be here.

It’s a real pleasure. I’ve been thinking lately, my family ranges from about twenty years old to, well I’m about eight years your senior. And we all really like your music. And I’ve been trying to figure out how you manage to do that.

Oh. I don’t know. But I’m glad too. I really like that about what’s been happening with the music is that we have children and old folks and everything in between that like it. That means a lot to us.
